title: Grade 11 Mathematics — Conic Sections
description: Conic Sections — circle, parabola, ellipse, hyperbola (CBSE Ch. 10)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The standard equation of a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r is:
questions.explanation: The standard form of a circle with centre (h, k) and radius r is (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r². For a circle centred at the origin, this simplifies to x² + y² = r².

The standard equation of a parabola with vertex at origin opening to the right is:
questions.explanation: y² = 4ax (a > 0) is a parabola opening to the right with vertex at origin, focus at (a, 0), and directrix x = −a. y² = −4ax opens to the left; x² = 4ay opens upward.

questions.question: For the parabola y² = 12x, the focus is at:
questions.explanation: y² = 12x → 4a = 12 → a = 3. The focus is at (a, 0) = (3, 0). The directrix is x = −3.

questions.question: The standard equation of an ellipse with semi-major axis a (along x-axis) and semi-minor axis b is:
questions.explanation: Standard ellipse: x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a > b > 0). The major axis is along the x-axis; vertices at (±a, 0); co-vertices at (0, ±b); foci at (±c, 0) where c² = a² − b².

questions.question: For the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1, the eccentricity e is:
questions.explanation: a² = 25, b² = 9 → c² = a² − b² = 16 → c = 4. Eccentricity e = c/a = 4/5. (For an ellipse, 0 < e < 1.)

questions.question: The foci of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 are at:
questions.explanation: From above: c = 4. Foci are at (±c, 0) = (±4, 0).

questions.question: The standard equation of a hyperbola with transverse axis along the x-axis is:
questions.explanation: x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 (a, b > 0) is a hyperbola with transverse axis along the x-axis. Vertices at (±a, 0); foci at (±c, 0) where c² = a² + b². For c² = a² − b², that would be an ellipse.

questions.question: For a hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1, the asymptotes are:
questions.explanation: The asymptotes of x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 are y = ±(b/a)x. As x → ∞, the hyperbola approaches these lines but never touches them.

questions.question: The eccentricity of a parabola is:
questions.explanation: Eccentricity e: circle = 0, ellipse = (0,1), parabola = 1 (exactly), hyperbola > 1. The parabola is the conic section with e = 1 — every point is equidistant from the focus and directrix.

questions.question: The length of the latus rectum of the parabola y² = 4ax is:
questions.explanation: The latus rectum is the chord through the focus perpendicular to the axis. For y² = 4ax, its length = 4a. (The endpoints are (a, 2a) and (a, −2a).)

questions.question: If the foci of an ellipse are at (±3, 0) and a vertex is at (5, 0), the equation is:
questions.explanation: a = 5 (vertex), c = 3 (focus). b² = a² − c² = 25 − 9 = 16. Equation: x²/25 + y²/16 = 1.

questions.question: The hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1 has eccentricity:
questions.explanation: a² = 9, b² = 16 → c² = a² + b² = 25 → c = 5. e = c/a = 5/3. (For a hyperbola, e > 1, so 5/3 is correct.)

questions.question: The sum of the distances from any point on an ellipse to its two foci equals:
questions.explanation: By the definition of an ellipse: for any point P on the ellipse, PF₁ + PF₂ = 2a (the length of the major axis). This is the focal property of the ellipse.

questions.question: A circle has the equation x² + y² = 36. A point (6, 0) lies on the circle. The tangent at this point is:
questions.explanation: For a circle x² + y² = r², the tangent at point (x₁, y₁) is xx₁ + yy₁ = r². Here: x·6 + y·0 = 36 → 6x = 36 → x = 6.
